The first stages of Arabidopsiss embryogenesis, which include the specification of the outer layer, the ground tissue, the shoot domain and the root domain, and the establishment of stem cells, are controlled by a combination of transcription factors and signalling pathways.
The first cell fate specification events in the plant embryo occur during the early globular stage, when stem cells are first established and all the major tissues of the plant are specified.
the first cell fate decisions in Arabidopsis embryonic development are controlled by the interplay between the transcription factors WUSCHEL and SHOOTMERISTEMLESS and the microRNAs miR165/6.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that control the formation of tissues and organs in the developing embryo and how these processes are conserved in the adult plant.
understanding how the major tissues and cell types in plants are specified and how they become patterned.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the specification of the major lineages of plant embryos occurs by a combination of cell autonomous mechanisms, and non-autonomous signals that are generated from the surrounding tissue.

the specification of all major cell types and tissues in the early plant embryo is dependent on the activity of the transcription factor WUSCHEL (WUS) and its downstream target, the transcriptional regulator SHORTROOT (SHR), which is expressed in the ground tissue of the embryo.
the specification of the outer and inner layers is dependent upon auxin, whereas the specification of the ground and vascular tissues is dependent on the activity of the auxin efflux carrier PIN1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the early embryo is a dynamic system, with the specification of cell fates occurring in a stepwise manner.
the early stages of embryogenesis in Arabidopsis involve a combination of positional information and cell-cell communication to establish a pattern of cell fate specification.
cell fates are determined by a balance of positive and negative regulators, with the final cell identity resulting from a combination of cell autonomous and non-cell-autonomous signalling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same genetic pathways are reused during embryogenesis and post-embryogenesis, with a few additional genes required for embryogenesis.
the specification of the first stem cell is a key event that is central to the establishment of the embryo's body plan.
, despite the simplicity of the early embryo, there are many different mechanisms that are employed to specify the different cell fates.
